data.title: OS Command Injection in Ping Tool (/ping)
data.description: The Flask Ping Tool passes user-supplied input from the `ip_address` POST parameter directly into an OS shell command without sanitization. An attacker can append arbitrary shell commands using semicolons (`;`) or other shell metacharacters, achieving full Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server.

## Flag Found

**`flag{e10ecfcb-fa35-4d78-9b28-5e922c08349d}`**

---

### Summary

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Target** | `http://172.17.0.1:48109` — Flask/Werkzeug 3.0.6 Ping Tool |
| **Vulnerability** | OS Command Injection — CRITICAL |
| **Endpoint** | `POST /ping` — `ip_address` parameter |
| **Payload** | `ip_address=127.0.0.1; cat /FLAG.txt` |
| **Flag location** | `/FLAG.txt` (filesystem root) |
| **Flag** | `flag{e10ecfcb-fa35-4d78-9b28-5e922c08349d}` |

**Attack chain:** The `ip_address` field was passed unsanitized into a shell command (`ping -c 2 <input>`). Appending `; find / -name FLAG.txt` revealed the file at `/FLAG.txt`, then `; cat /FLAG.txt` extracted the flag in a single request. PoC saved to `pocs/20260412_214802_cmdi-ping-flag-extraction.http`.
